purpose: Add proportional product, architecture, data, quality, review, and lifecycle assurance to repositories that build maintained software applications with AI agents.

criteria: The project builds or maintains a software application whose user workflows, data, or release claims need review beyond the universal workflow core.
The project can run Node.js for the structural contract check or explicitly records that environment gate as open.
evidence: The ToVA Operations Command Center contract proves same-source app intent can link product workflows to existing source and acceptance evidence.
The founder-friendly app-building review identified product, data, migration, performance, security/privacy, testing, and lifecycle checks not owned by the universal core.

non_goals: Do not replace the product goal, architecture, active task, Project Health, source code, or acceptance owners.
Do not require one UI-controller-service-repository class structure for every application.
Do not turn a structural contract pass into runtime, device, human, privacy, migration, beta, or release acceptance.

preserve: Project-owned app.build.json contracts that remain linked from current source or acceptance owners.
Accepted assurance evidence needed to explain historical beta, release, migration, or human decisions.
